newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel stands by quick punishment for EMU sins.
newsitem.headline: Waigel stands by quick punishment for EMU sins.

text.p: German Finance Minster Theo Waigel on Friday stood by his frequently-repeated call for quick sanctions for violators of fiscal discipline once European Union members adopt a single currency.

"The near automatic implementation of sanction is a part of the stability pact in my opinion," Waigel said according to the text of a speech to be held at a meeting of the German Chemical Industry Federation in Frankfurt.
Waigel stands by quick punishment for EMU sins

Waigel said that every member of the European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) whose budget deficit exceeds the ceiling of three percent of gross domestic product should make an interest-free deposit with the European Union.
Should the country exceed the criteria set out in the Maastricht Treaty again within two years the deposit would be automatically turned over to the EU as a penalty.
"Near automatic sanctions are favoured as a deterrent element to ensure budget discipline," Waigel said.
European Union members that meet the strict fiscal criteria will give up their national currencies in 1999 and adopt the Euro, that will eventually become Europe's single currency.

Waigel repeated his insistence that adhering to the fiscal criteria should have priority over timetable for monetary union and said there was no dicussion among European finance ministers about weakening the EMU criteria.
